title: Decentralized community resource cooperation
original_statement: I propose that a community may distribute shared resources through local cooperation between individuals rather than depending entirely on a central authority.

revisions.change_summary: Initial capture of the original idea.
revisions.working_statement: I propose that a community may distribute shared resources through local cooperation between individuals rather than depending entirely on a central authority.

revisions.change_summary: Identify initial concepts, a real-world analogy, assumptions and unresolved operational questions.
revisions.working_statement: A community may coordinate the allocation of finite shared resources through local cooperation between individuals, without relying entirely on a central authority. The conditions and rules governing cooperation remain to be defined.

concepts.name: Community
concepts.definition: A group of individuals participating in a shared resource arrangement.

concepts.name: Individual
concepts.definition: A participant who can contribute to and receive shared resources.

concepts.name: Shared resource pool
concepts.definition: A finite collection of resources available to the community.
concepts.source_note: Mapped provisionally to common-pool resource arrangements.

concepts.name: Collective trust
concepts.definition: A proposed concept describing confidence between participants.

concepts.name: Local coordination
concepts.definition: A proposed way for participants to coordinate contributions and allocation.
concepts.source_note: Suggested during concept decomposition; requires user review.

properties.name: Available quantity
properties.definition: Quantity currently available in the shared pool.

properties.name: Trust level
properties.definition: A conceptual property whose measurement is not yet specified.

relationships.label: participates in
relationships.description: An individual participates in the community arrangement.

relationships.label: contributes to
relationships.description: An individual may contribute resources to the shared pool.

relationships.label: may influence
relationships.description: Collective trust may influence local coordination.

mechanisms.name: Cooperative resource allocation
mechanisms.description: Participants coordinate local contributions and allocation decisions.
mechanisms.trigger_description: A participant requests or contributes resources.
mechanisms.effect_description: The community's allocation state may change.

hypotheses.statement: Under some conditions, resource scarcity may increase cooperation between participants.

assumptions.statement: Participants can observe at least some information about shared resource availability.
assumptions.rationale: This assumption is needed to reason about local allocation decisions.

constraints.statement: The shared resource pool is finite at any given time.
constraints.rationale: The theory concerns allocation under resource limits.

mappings.rationale: This is a candidate analogy for thinking about shared resources; it is not evidence that the proposed theory works.
mappings.target_description: Real-world arrangements in which multiple participants draw on a shared resource system.

open_questions.question: How should collective trust be represented or measured?
What specific rule determines how resources are allocated when requests exceed availability?
